VeraGridEngine.Simulations.EMT.emt_problem_factory module

VeraGridEngine.Simulations.EMT.emt_problem_factory.build_emt_problem(grid: MultiCircuit, options: EmtOptions, pf_results: PowerFlowResults | None = None, pf_results_3ph: PowerFlowResults3Ph | None = None, progress_signal: DummySignal | None = None, logger: Logger | None = None) → EmtProblemDae[source]

Build the EMT problem implementation selected in the simulation options.

Parameters:

  • grid – Electrical grid whose devices define the EMT problem.

  • options – EMT configuration, including the requested problem type.

  • pf_results – Optional balanced power-flow initialization results.

  • pf_results_3ph – Optional three-phase power-flow initialization results.

  • progress_signal – Optional signal used to publish numeric progress.

  • logger – Optional logger owned by the simulation driver.

Returns:

Configured EMT problem ready to be passed to a solver.

class VeraGridEngine.Simulations.EMT.initialization_emt.EmtPseudoTransientProblemAdapter(reduced_system: ReducedInitializationSystem, problem: EmtProblemTemplate, x_full: ndarray, dx_full: ndarray, runtime_params: ndarray, constant_params: ndarray)[source]

Bases: RmsProblemTemplate

Adapt one EMT reduced initialization system to the RMS pseudo-transient solver API.

The RMS pseudo-transient implementation expects a problem object exposing the RMS numerical interface. This adapter provides that interface on top of the EMT reduced initialization residual and Jacobian so the EMT initializer can reuse the existing pseudo-transient algorithm without changing the solver.

VeraGridEngine.Simulations.EMT.initialization_emt.init_pseudo_transient(problem: EmtProblemTemplate, options: EmtOptions) → EmtInitializationReport[source]

Run the EMT-native initialization workflow forcing the pure pseudo-transient path.

This helper does not execute explicit initialization. It starts from the current problem seed, which in the main EMT build workflow corresponds to the power-flow projected variables.

Parameters:

  • problem – EMT problem being initialized.

  • options – EMT simulation options.

Returns:

Initialization report.

VeraGridEngine.Simulations.EMT.initialization_emt.run_emt_device_pseudo_transient_initialization(problem: EmtProblemTemplate, blocks: List[Block], options: EmtOptions, check_kcl: bool = True) → EmtInitializationReport[source]

Solve each complete device at a balanced periodic PF operating point.

Device registration and residuals use only dynamic equations. Machine and controller children share one solve. PF terminal voltages remain fixed and mapped terminal currents anchor the operating point. Unseeded Const(None) event parameters become unknown references; symbolic references also carry their defining residual. Neither init_eqs nor diff_init_eqs is evaluated.

Pseudo time relaxes f(x)-D_periodic(x)=0. ABC state triples use their fundamental sinusoidal derivatives; dq/controller states use zero and absolute rotor angles advance at grid frequency. This balanced fundamental approximation is checked against the assembled DAE at four cycle phases.

VeraGridEngine.Simulations.EMT.initialization_emt.run_emt_native_initialization(problem: EmtProblemTemplate, options: EmtOptions) → EmtInitializationReport[source]

Run the EMT-native initialization stages after power-flow variable projection.

The workflow keeps the current seed intact, then solves only the unresolved subset with the native initialization algorithm requested by options.initialization_method. The concrete EMT build uses device-local periodic pseudo-transient initialization directly from PF seeds for PseudoTransient; this native dispatcher remains available for direct helper calls and the other initialization methods. Missing differential initial values are computed automatically from the state equations.

Parameters:

  • problem – EMT problem being initialized.

  • options – EMT simulation options.

Returns:

Initialization report.
